W.note: Solid sequential-impulse solver with sleeping and Coulomb friction and a direct, throwable drag, but the only control is Reset and there is no hint text, so the task is not obvious.

X.note: Spring-driven drag with throw, click-to-add, gravity toggle and HUD text make it the most usable, though boxes are axis-aligned with no rotation and the HUD overlaps boxes on phone width.

Y.note: Most believable physics (SAT oriented boxes with rotation, friction, restitution, sleeping, spring grab with a visible tether and throw), but it offers only Reset and no hint, so it is hard to discover.

Z.note: Substepped 1/240 solver with friction, a kinematic drag that throws, and Add/Reset/Clear with a count and hint, though the hint overlaps the stack on phone width and boxes do not rotate.
